name: Name expressiveness (information density)
articulated_construct: Beyond casing and blacklist checks, identifier names should carry phrase-level information through their morphemes and vocabulary, should be specific enough for the scope in which they operate, and should avoid terse or filler surfaces such as x, tmp, or data when those surfaces erase distinctions needed by readers.

axes.articulability: A prompt-based implementation can interpret whether a name fits the surrounding program concept.
axes.verifiability: A code-based implementation can expose identifier surfaces, lexical scopes, declarations, uses, collisions, and shadowing.
axes.isomorphism: Prompt and code implementations must consume the exact same sanitized_ctext and articulated construct; agreement is measured independently from capability on either axis.

representation.representation_policy: TRAIN, prompt, code, and heldout paths must call the same frozen projection hook before consuming ctext.
representation.comparison_policy: A historical comparator over raw text is not representation-identical for changed rows. The primary prompt comparator must be freshly produced over the same sanitized_ctext.
not_available: unchanged declarations and uses outside diff context

executable_evidence: path and enclosing language-aware lexical scopes
scope depth and added-fragment line span
resolved use count and lexical reach within visible added code
projected_relations.interpretive_boundary: The appropriate amount of specificity and any eventual scope weights are not frozen by the capability.

executable_evidence: snake-case, camel-case, acronym, and digit morpheme segmentation
surface and morpheme counts available for later aggregation
fragment-local vocabulary diversity available for later aggregation
projected_relations.interpretive_boundary: Lexical diversity is surface evidence, not proof that the information is relevant or correct.

executable_evidence: language-aware scope span and resolved-use evidence
projected_relations.interpretive_boundary: Short conventional names can be appropriate in tiny mathematical, iterator, callback, or receiver scopes.

executable_evidence: declarations with no resolved uses in visible added code
projected_relations.interpretive_boundary: Fragment-local unresolved or unused status may be caused by unchanged code outside the diff.

executable_evidence: multiple declaration events for the same name in one qualified scope
a nested declaration sharing a name with a visible ancestor declaration
projected_relations.interpretive_boundary: The relations are mechanically detectable within supported fragments, but harmfulness remains language- and context-dependent.
Whether a name denotes the right domain concept or communicates intent requires semantic interpretation absent from the structural capability.

language_rules: Python member and subscript assignment targets are not lexical bindings
Python named redefinitions remain distinct while repeated lexical rebinding sites coalesce
Python function lookup skips intervening class namespaces
JavaScript and TypeScript let and const bind to blocks while var binds to function or file scope
Go var, short-var, range, receiver, and parameter bindings are represented
type identifiers are excluded from lexical-use events

synthetic_contrast_probes.contrast: self.timeout assignment versus timeout lexical assignment
two same-name functions versus two assignment sites for one lexical name
nested let shadowing versus nested var function binding
parameters, var declarations, and short-var declarations versus type identifiers

claim_boundary: This contract projects articulated sub-relations into executable facts. It does not freeze an a407 metric, establish isomorphism, validate disagreement correctness, or treat failed reconstruction as evidence of tacitness.
